findings.title: Loopback model endpoint can redirect prompt data to an external host
findings.what: Only the initial endpoint is passed through chatCompletionsUrl/assertLoopbackEndpoint. The subsequent fetch does not set redirect:'manual'; standard fetch follows redirects. A loopback service can return a 307/308 redirect to a non-loopback URL, preserving the POST body containing model messages and defeating the stated local-only LLM-egress guardrail.
findings.fix: Set redirect:'manual' (or 'error') on the request and reject redirect responses. If redirects are required, follow them explicitly only after revalidating every Location target as loopback.
findings.acceptance: A test fetch implementation or local fixture returning a 307/308 Location to https://example.invalid must result in LocalModelError and must make no request to the redirected host; a normal loopback 200 response must still succeed.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the only host validation occurs before fetch at line 159, while the fetch options at lines 174-185 contain no redirect policy or post-redirect URL validation.

findings.title: Corpus validation can approve tasks that do not round-trip unchanged
findings.what: validateCorpus claims validity requires an unchanged parser round-trip, but it compares only task counts. Inputs normalized without being dropped—such as a non-integer expectExitCode defaulted to 0, trimmed text, duplicate/oversized tags, or an omitted tags field—retain the same count and are incorrectly reported valid. A caller can consequently execute or record different gate semantics from the parser's canonical form.
findings.fix: Compare the complete reparsed corpus with the supplied corpus using a deterministic deep equality check and report field-level normalization/drift, while retaining the existing malformed/duplicate count error.
findings.acceptance: Add tests where a one-task corpus has expectExitCode:1.5, padded text, duplicate tags, and missing tags; validateCorpus must return ok:false for each, while CURATED_CORPUS remains ok:true.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed parseObjectiveGate normalizes invalid expectExitCode to 0 and parseTags normalizes tags, while validateCorpus at lines 183-187 observes only reparsed.length; the existing success test does not exercise normalization drift.

findings.title: Routing recommendations are accepted and promoted without reproducible provenance
findings.what: The sanitizer accepts a recommendation's modelId, scope, weightedScore, evidence-strength label, and rationale independently of sanitized runs. Ingest then keeps and emits the highest such score without verifying matching model/scope evidence, veto state, or carrying the source artifact's createdAt/batchPath. An untrusted artifact can therefore inject an unsupported recommendation, and historical claims are emitted without an 'as of' timestamp or structured artifact provenance.
findings.fix: Define structured recommendation provenance containing the supporting artifact and run/evidence identifiers; derive or verify recommendation score and strongestEvidence from matching sanitized runs, reject recommendations contradicted by vetoes or lacking support, and retain createdAt/batchPath (or an explicit asOf field) in the summary recommendation.
findings.acceptance: A forged recommendation with no matching run/evidence, a score inconsistent with its supporting run, or a vetoed supporting run must be rejected. A valid recommendation must round-trip with run/evidence references plus batchPath and asOf/createdAt, and the summary must expose those fields.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed sanitizeRecommendation performs only scalar/type/enum checks, while ingest compares the supplied weightedScore and evidence rank directly. Neither stage cross-references artifact.runs, and the emitted recommendation omits the artifact ledger's createdAt and batchPath.
